findings.affected_surface: Public GLib/GObject/GIO C API - glib public header
findings.old_behavior: GUserDirectory enum has members DESKTOP through VIDEOS (8 members). G_USER_N_DIRECTORIES sentinel equals 8. Any code iterating i=0..G_USER_N_DIRECTORIES-1 processes 8 directories.
findings.new_behavior: GUserDirectory enum gains G_USER_DIRECTORY_PROJECTS after VIDEOS. G_USER_N_DIRECTORIES sentinel now equals 9. Code iterating i=0..G_USER_N_DIRECTORIES-1 processes 9 directories, including the new PROJECTS slot. Code that statically initializes arrays of size G_USER_N_DIRECTORIES will have one extra element.
findings.compatibility_reason: Adding a new enum value at the end of GUserDirectory changes the integer value of G_USER_N_DIRECTORIES from 8 to 9. This is an ABI change: any existing compiled code that uses G_USER_N_DIRECTORIES as an array bound or loop sentinel will have a mismatched size when linked against the new library. C code compiled with the old header that uses switch() without default will not handle the new value. The enum documentation explicitly states 'The #GUserDirectory enumeration can be extended at later date', so this is an expected additive change, but still a binary-incompatible sentinel shift for any code compiled against the old header and linked against the new library.

evidence.snippet:
G_USER_DIRECTORY_TEMPLATES,
  G_USER_DIRECTORY_VIDEOS,

  /**
   * G_USER_DIRECTORY_PROJECTS:
   *
   * The user's Projects directory.
   *
   * Since: 2.90
   */
  G_USER_DIRECTORY_PROJECTS,

  G_USER_N_DIRECTORIES
} GUserDirectory;

findings.why_not_internal_only: glib/gutils.h is a public installed header installed via pkg-config (glib-2.0.pc). The GUserDirectory enum and its sentinel G_USER_N_DIRECTORIES are part of the public GLib C API surface, documented and used by application code.
findings.uncertainty: The enum is explicitly documented as extensible, so some consumers may already handle unknown values gracefully. However, G_USER_N_DIRECTORIES is a sentinel used for array sizing and loop bounds, and changing its value is a binary-level ABI break regardless of documentation intent.
findings.recommended_review: Verify that downstream consumers that use G_USER_N_DIRECTORIES as a fixed array size or switch boundary handle the new enum value gracefully. Check that GLib's own internal g_user_special_dirs array (sized by G_USER_N_DIRECTORIES) is correctly sized everywhere it is allocated or referenced.
findings.test_recommendation: Write a regression test that iterates all GUserDirectory values from 0 to G_USER_N_DIRECTORIES-1 and calls g_get_user_special_dir() for each, verifying that the new PROJECTS slot returns a valid path (or NULL if not configured). Verify that g_icon_name lookups for the PROJECTS path return the expected icon. Recompile existing test suites against the new header to catch any array-size mismatch.

findings.affected_surface: GIO behavior - file info icon lookup
findings.old_behavior: When the path matches G_USER_DIRECTORY_PICTURES but not any earlier directory check, the if-else chain falls through to the else clause returning NULL. The projects directory path (if PROJECTS were resolvable by some other means) would result in no icon name match.
findings.new_behavior: When the path matches g_get_user_special_dir(G_USER_DIRECTORY_PROJECTS), the new else-if branch returns 'folder-projects-symbolic' or 'folder-projects' as the icon name instead of falling through to NULL. The observable effect is that g_file_query_info() on a path matching the projects directory now returns an icon instead of no icon.
findings.compatibility_reason: This is an additive behavioral change: a new code path is added for the new G_USER_DIRECTORY_PROJECTS enum value. Existing compiled code can only reach this new code path if it is recompiled with the new header (to access G_USER_DIRECTORY_PROJECTS) or if it iterates over all G_USER_N_DIRECTORIES values. The change is triggered by the new enum value being used as an argument to g_get_user_special_dir(). Since the icon is returned via g_file_info_set_icon() / g_file_info_set_symbolic_icon(), any application that queries file info and displays icons may now show a different icon for the projects directory.
findings.why_not_internal_only: Although get_icon_name is static, it is called by get_icon() which is called by _g_local_file_info_get(), the backend for the public g_file_query_info() API. The icon name change propagates to the public GFileInfo icon attributes (G_FILE_ATTRIBUTE_ID_STANDARD_ICON and G_FILE_ATTRIBUTE_ID_STANDARD_SYMBOLIC_ICON), making this a user-visible behavioral change.
findings.uncertainty: This code path is only reachable when the input path matches g_get_user_special_dir(G_USER_DIRECTORY_PROJECTS). If no system/user config sets XDG_PROJECTS_DIR, g_get_user_special_dir() returns NULL and this branch is never taken (g_strcmp0 handles NULL safely). The actual observable impact depends on whether end users configure the XDG_PROJECTS_DIR environment variable or user-dirs.dirs entry.
findings.recommended_review: Verify that the 'folder-projects' and 'folder-projects-symbolic' icon names are available in the installed icon theme. If the icon names are not present in common icon themes (Adwaita, Humanity), the returned GIcon may be a fallback or empty, which could cause degraded display in file managers.
findings.test_recommendation: Write a test that sets XDG_PROJECTS_DIR to a temporary directory, calls g_file_query_info() on that directory, and verifies that the returned icon name contains 'folder-projects'. Also verify that the icon is non-NULL and has a non-empty name.
